metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: does a repeatable, domain-specific Claude capability like client-review mean Claude is analyzing the portfolio and deciding what matters for the meeting, or is it just a plain-text file of instructions Claude reads and follows? beats.narration_text: Someone assumed Claude's client-review capability was a built-in portfolio analysis app. It isn't — it's a plain-text skill Claude reads. So: does Claude's client-review skill analyze the portfolio, or does it just assemble the meeting?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 1.0 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('app' -> 'skill') lands on screen and the full corrected question finishes typing before the clip ends. Text/rates copied from the already-validated hai-simple fix pattern (42ms/char, 4% mistakeRate, 8% hesitateBetween) proven on the client-report and agent-development siblings, to avoid repeating their first-attempt slower/higher-rate timeout.

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it works. This one is client-review. The SKILL.md file holds the full instruction set — plain language, no hidden logic. Claude reads it, then acts. The file is the program.
The pipeline lives in the file's Steps section. Claude reads the file, runs each step in order, and returns the result — linear, no branching unless a step itself says so.

Client-review's SKILL.md spells out exactly what to produce: a portfolio performance summary, allocation analysis, talking points, and action items, ready before quarterly reviews, annual checkups, or an ad-hoc client meeting. Feed it the same account data twice, and it builds the same meeting-ready packet twice. Ask for something the file doesn't cover — a comparison it never mentions, a chart it doesn't list — and there's no instruction to fall back on, so Claude reasons past the file on its own.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: write a SKILL.md for a recurring meeting you prep for. List exactly what must appear every time, then list what would be left to my judgment because the file doesn't cover it. Read back what Claude wrote — the first list is what repeats identically every run; the second is where it's reasoning past the file, not following it.
